steps.scene: You're following two cyclists towards a roundabout. Both are in the left-hand lane, keeping well over to the kerb.

question.prompt: Which way should you expect them to go?

options.text: Left — that's the lane they're in
Any direction
Straight ahead only

question.explanation: Cyclists often stay left the whole way round because crossing the traffic feels unsafe — even when turning right.

steps.title: A cyclist signalling right
steps.body: They need space and time to take their line across the roundabout. Hold back and leave them room — don't try to help them along.

question.prompt: A cyclist ahead of you signals right at a roundabout. What should you do?

options.text: Signal them across so they know you've seen them
Overtake on their right while there's room
Give them plenty of room and stay back

question.explanation: Room and patience are all they need. A wave from you could send them across the path of a car you can't see.

steps.scene: A horse and rider are ahead of you at a roundabout. The rider is signalling right, but staying well over to the left.

options.text: Stay well back and let them go at their own pace
Treat the left-hand position as the real intention
Move up close so they know you're waiting

question.explanation: Horses move slowly and often keep left all the way round. Close or alongside will unsettle the horse.

steps.title: A rider in the middle of the lane
steps.body: On a narrow road a rider may take the centre deliberately. It makes them visible and stops you squeezing past where there's no room.

question.prompt: A horse rider ahead is riding in the centre of a narrow lane. You should…

options.text: Ease past on the right where the road allows
Stay behind and let them ride in that position
Move up close to encourage them to pull aside

question.explanation: It's a safety position, not bad manners. Wait until there's genuine room, then pass slowly and wide.

steps.title: The box between two stop lines
steps.body: At some lights a marked area sits between two stop lines. It's reserved for cyclists, so they can wait ahead of the traffic and be seen.

question.prompt: What is the marked area between the two stop lines for?

options.text: It's spare space any vehicle may wait in
To let cyclists wait in front of other traffic
To let people cross the road between the lines

question.explanation: Stop at the first line. If the lights changed as you crossed it, stop at the second — but don't aim for the box.

steps.scene: You're driving past a line of parked cars. Between two of them you catch sight of a bicycle wheel, pointing out into the road.

options.text: Nothing — it's a parked bike between the cars
Slow down, ready to stop for a cyclist pulling out
Sound your horn and keep your speed up past them

question.explanation: Read the part you can see. A wheel at that angle is a cyclist about to join the road in front of you.

steps.title: Loose animals in the road
steps.body: Sheep or cattle in the road are easily panicked by engine noise and close passes. Go very slowly, and stop if the person in charge signals you.

question.prompt: How should you pass loose sheep on the road?

options.text: Sound your horn briefly to move them along
Quickly but quietly, so you're past sooner
Very slowly, ready to stop

question.explanation: Noise scatters animals into the road rather than out of it. Crawl past, and be ready to stop and wait.
